keyFindings.description: Fast-follow, judged below the round-4 bar and named in the approval. askIdentity joins a block's id and its opening with NUL characters and nothing stops the opening from holding one, so a block with no id whose text begins `first\u0000Keep it unchanged.` gets the key of the block `#first` whose text is `Keep it unchanged.`; I reproduced the collision through newAsks at this head, and both thermonuclear agents found it independently. Two refusals of the forged ask would then pass the real one unreviewed. It is below the bar for three reasons together, each checked: on the bash surface, the only one a Legion pod has and the only one four rounds could drive, a NUL makes the write unreadable (hasControlCharacter at :683 through headLine at :537 and :941) and an unreadable scoped write is refused, so the seed cannot be sent there at all; on the device surface, which no Legion pod mounts, it needs the gated agent to type NULs on purpose and buys it nothing, since advisor_rebuttal already sends any one call unreviewed in one step; and the forged pass is still recorded as outcome breaker and announced to the agent. The remedy is one line — JSON.stringify([kind, id ?? null, opening]), keeping the no-id case on the opening alone — with a regression that refuses the NUL seed twice and asserts the ordinary #first block is still reviewed.

notes: Approved at the head the handoff push made, with the code at 34920d4b1caa90dc7d84faedda408ab1e7c9ed47 and only .legion/ paths above it. CI read on GitHub, not from a handoff: main's rulesets require lint, typecheck, test and pr-title, branch protection names none, and all four are completed and success at that commit; the non-required pi-envoy lane, which carries A1's pin beside test, is success too.

Round 3's three narrowed items are closed, each verified here rather than read off a commit message. The breaker collapse: newAsks at this head gives two distinct identities for two same-text blocks with different ids where round 3 gave one, while a resend of one block, a block whose tail is reworded, and a dispatch ask whose tail is reworded all keep one identity, so the dedupe and the id key did not buy the fix at the cost of the termination the opening gives. The unjudged path: I read the day back myself with askgate-report.ts --dispatch-project INFRA --since 2026-10-25T09:06:00Z and it prints `rules calls that judged none of their asks: 1 (pod 1, machine 0)` beside `partial: 1`, where that line read 0 in each of the three earlier rounds — a real record, not a line that prints zero. The README sentence now says what the code says.

The architect's ruling on the rules call timing out at 120 and 220 asks is accepted as a risk line, and the evidence supports it rather than only the argument: round 3's 40,195-byte single-ask edit and 36,611-byte twelve-block edit carried the same request bytes and did not time out, both ending in a rule match, so the timeout tracks the number of asks rather than a size an ordinary write reaches. It also fails visibly — ruleOutcome timeout, counted by the reader, which my own read shows at 2 with a 40% error rate for that window — and the charter refused both runs for its own reasons, so no ask reached a person unjudged in either.

The implementer's correction landed and is true: the body now names the two asks its probe upload opened (2b6b90bb and e5d362fb) and says they are retracted, and dispatch read of INFRA-373 shows `Open asks: none` with both resolved and the fixture closed.

Both thermonuclear agents ran at the reviewed head; the deep review approved and the quality review requested changes, and their one finding is the same NUL collision above, which I reproduced before judging it. The deep review's mutation runs are worth recording: removing the dedupe fails test 14h, reverting the id key fails 14i, reverting both fails 14f, 14h and 14i, and the unmutated suite passes 224 of 224 — so each half of the fix carries a test that fails without it. Its second note, that a block resent under a new id each time starts a new thing and is reviewed again, fails toward more review and not less.
Threads: all five carry an answer from both sides and are resolved. The two the reviewer reopened at round 3, PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v-tYH and PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v-tYJ, are answered again here and accepted.

Fast-follow carried into the approval, none of it blocking: the NUL identity encoding above; askgate-report.ts accepting --sessions '' where --dispatch-project '' is refused by name; two id-less ask blocks of one call still sharing an identity, which the dedupe now makes harmless within a call; and the rules call's timeout at a write of more than a hundred ask blocks.
